sessions.title: RACE DAY
sessions.detail: Garden Route Triathlon Ultra - 2 km swim, 80 km bike, 20 km run.

effort.note: Race effort is not 'how fast can I go'. It is the hardest pace you could hold all day and still run at the end of it. For the first hour it should feel frustratingly easy. Heart rate is the master control on every surface; pace and speed drift with wind, gradient, heat and fatigue.

surfaces.cue: Full sentences at race effort. If you cannot, you are over.
Do not surge over the top. Keep pedalling on the descent.
Indoors runs 3-5 bpm HIGH for the same effort - no airflow. Subtract 5 bpm from road targets, or put a fan on.
Three or four words at a time. Off the bike, the first 2 km always feel strange.
A flat treadmill is easier than road. Set 1% and the pace numbers transfer.
Do not look at heart rate in the water. It lies.
Most of your time loss is swimming further than 2 km, not swimming slowly.

race_day.note: Settle for 200 m. Everyone else goes out too hard.
Short sentences, five to eight words.
Spin. Save it for the run.
Legs feel strange. It passes. Do not judge your day on it.
Run 9 min, walk 1 min through aid stations. From km 1, not km 14.
The only place you empty the tank.

fuel.daily: Eating at 3,000+ kcal with protein at 160-180 g and carbohydrate deliberately high. The cut is off until 20 September - you cannot absorb a peak block and a deficit at the same time.

rows.what: Rice, potatoes, oats, pasta, fruit. Protein 160-180 g across the day.
Same foods, smaller portions. Protein does not drop.
Oats with honey and banana, white bread with jam, coffee. Nothing high-fibre, nothing new.
A gel, or a few mouthfuls of your carb mix.
Two 750 ml bottles at 90 g each, plus two gels. Keep near 2:1 glucose:fructose - sucrose gets you there naturally.
A gel every 25-30 min, water at every aid station. Coke from 12 km if the stomach is holding.
Cool spring morning - stay at the low end. Do not over-drink.

rehab.what: Right ankle - sore on rotation since 31 August, worse after the 10 km treadmill run on 3 September. Fine when stable.
rehab.status: NOT ASSESSED. This has progressed, and it is the one thing that can end the race.
rules: Nothing that reproduces the twisting pain. Pain-free range only, every exercise.
Sharp pain means stop, not push through. Dull stretch is fine.
Do the block twice a day - once in the morning, once after training.
If it is worse the morning after a run, cut the next run and say so.

exercises.how: Trace A-Z with the toes, foot off the ground. Range you own without pain, not the range you want.

Foot flat, drive the knee past the toes toward the wall without the heel lifting. Measure the toe-to-wall gap on BOTH sides - the difference between them is your progress marker, not the absolute number. A right side more than 2 cm short of the left is the thing to close.
Three seconds up, three down. Progress to single leg only when 3 x 15 is easy and pain-free.
Up on two feet, down on one, over a step. Lower for four seconds. This is the one that actually builds tendon.
Light band, foot turns out then in against it. Slow, controlled, small range. This is the direct answer to a rotation problem.
Barefoot on the floor, then on a cushion. Proprioception is what stops the next roll.
Toes drag a towel toward you. Boring, and it works on the small stabilisers nothing else reaches.

reasonable.note: Needs piperine or a bioavailable formulation - kitchen turmeric absorbs poorly. Evidence is modest and mostly from osteoarthritis trials, but the risk is low.
Modest evidence for exercise soreness. Cheap and low risk.
Better evidence than the other two, slower to act.
After running or riding, not before.

anti_inflammatory.avoid: Ibuprofen and diclofenac taken orally to train or race through this. Two separate reasons: NSAIDs during prolonged endurance exercise raise the risk of acute kidney injury and exercise-associated hyponatremia, which is documented in long-course triathlon; and masking pain on an ankle nobody has examined is how a niggle becomes a real injury. Anything stronger is a conversation with a doctor, not with a training plan.

rehab.sides: Both ankles, every exercise. Three reasons: the left is your control, so the difference between sides is the number that actually tells you anything; training one side only builds an asymmetry you will feel at 15 km of a 20 km run; and the good ankle has been quietly compensating, so it has earned the work too. The right side sets the dose - do what the sore one can manage pain-free, and match it on the left.
